checked_and_found_correct: The mathematics, recomputed independently three times by three reviewers using methods sharing no code with the implementation — a closed-form chi-squared survival recurrence seeded by erfc/exp, a 200k-interval Simpson quadrature of the pdf, and an erfc-based Q(a,x) cross-check. All six probe p-values match every printed digit (0.135888, 0.091578, 0.061099, 0.220640, 0.075235, 0.061969), and the stored firing computes to 0.00101675 against a claimed 0.001017.

The article's spine: 5.991 sits below the true alpha=0.05 critical value for every df >= 4, verified by bisection to df=15, df=30 and df=200, and the critical value is strictly increasing in df — so the claim that the error had exactly one direction, manufacturing significance and never withholding it, holds universally rather than on the sampled points.

The one real firing. `{ chiSquared: 18.43, df: 4, pValue: '< 0.05', significant: true }` exists verbatim at /summary/statistics/modelComparison in overnight-multi-model-treatment-7iter-2026-02-09.json, and is the only df>=4 verdict among 3 chi-squared verdicts in 11 stored run files. Its verdict was correct anyway — the article's 'right answer from the wrong instrument' is exact, not rhetorical.
df = models.length - 1 is correct for an M x 2 contingency table, and the article deliberately declines to allege it as a second defect. Checked before the claim was not made.
Both quoted code blocks are byte-for-byte from b40bc6781, including that `pValue: 1` and the rendered-string `pValue` are two branches of the same function.
The absence result: the scoped six-term grep returns 0, and the article's own caveat about unscoped runs matching package-lock base64 reproduces at exactly 3.

The check fails on the unfixed state. Two reviewers independently reconstructed the old predicate and confirmed the ordering assertion p(6,4) > p(6,2) goes false and the run exits 1 — proven before the fix landed, not asserted after.

Identifier freeze, cover assets and outbound links: both images exist with slug-derived stems, all four outbound links resolve to on-disk articles that are published with devto_ids, and no dead forward-reference remains.

The `sdlc:verify` findings for this slug are verifier artifacts, not false claims — detect-stale-claims.mjs digit-strips a multi-assertion runner's stdout and lib.mjs splits on unescaped `|` inside markdown table cells. Every command it reports failing was hand-run in full by two reviewers and returns the stated value.

growth_hook.why: The title is technically exact and legible without the domain — df = models-1, so the 5.991 fallback is genuinely the three-model bar, and the mismatch reads on sight. The opening's payload travels standalone ('the one significance test I *did* have was a dictionary'), and the structure's bravest move is refusing its own best headline: 'It fired once, and got the right answer' converts the anticlimax into the thesis rather than burying it. Held below 10 because the real-world payoff is n=1 of eleven files and it was right anyway, so the stakes stay intellectual rather than consequential.

security_correctness.why: Every number recomputed by two methods sharing no code with the implementation, agreeing to every printed digit, including the 0.001017 firing and the bisected critical values 3.841/5.991/7.815/9.488/11.070. The one-directional-error claim was verified universally rather than on samples. The only softness is phrasing rather than arithmetic: 'reproduces 3.841, 5.991 and 7.815 to three decimals' describes recovering p=0.05 from those statistics rather than computing the critical values themselves.

structure_framing_voice.why: Every H2 is load-bearing — mechanism, measured frequency, direction of the error, why it survived review, then the second call site where extending the table moved the cliff without removing it, which is the line the piece turns on. Framing is landscape-only: zero banned-vocabulary hits, no external project named, and the only instrument criticised is our own. The negation-contrast construction runs about 1 per 120 words against 1 per 180 and 1 per 270 in the two published siblings — the densest of the three, staying signature because each instance draws a real technical distinction, except in 'The fix is arithmetic' where three run in four sentences and only the last carries meaning.

compatibility.why: All ten required frontmatter fields present; reading_time_minutes 6 is exactly the repo's own computation over 1,190 words. Both cover assets exist with correctly slug-derived stems and the conventional ?v=b2 buster; all four outbound links resolve to published articles with devto_ids; identifier freeze is clean with the rename completed while still legal.
